newsitem.title: USA: ABA sees US GDP rising, urges summer Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: ABA sees US GDP rising, urges summer Fed rate hike.

text.p: An American Bankers Association advisory committee said Thursday it expects U.S. economic growth to rebound from its current "lull."

In a forecast, the panel said it expects the economy to grow at a rate of less than two percent during the current quarter, but it predicted growth will accelerate to nearly three percent during the second half of 1997.
The bank economists also said that the Federal Reserve should raise short-term interest rates by at least 25 basis points "this summer."
Committee members said growth has exceeded expectations over the past year and created wage pressures that could threaten the current low level of inflation.
At the same time the panel cautioned that Fed action on interest rates "should be limited because long-term inflation prospects remain favorable."
The panel forecast consumer installment credit growth of six percent this year. It expects that growth rate to ease to five percent next year.

"Consumers' thirst for products has largely been quenched," said Joel Naroff, chief bank economist at First Union Corp and chairman of the ABA panel. "We will see single-digit growth rates of consumer credit this year and next, well below double-digit levels of previous years."
